To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
in patients with schizophrenia there is an increased activity of elastase and a significant increase of WF and C-RP concentrations in blood plasma.

the activity of LE and the concentrations of WF and C-RP in the blood plasma are increased in ALS schizophrenia patients compared to controls, and that these changes are positively correlated with severity of clinical symptoms.
in ALS schizophrenia the activity of leukocyte protease and markers of EC dysfunction are significantly increased.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the first evidence of the involvement of vascular endothelial lesion in the pathogenesis of ALS schizophrenia.
the first demonstration that the EC dysfunction and/or damage may play a significant role in the pathogenesis of ALS.
the hypothesis that ALS schizophrenia is accompanied by EC dysfunction and/or EC lesion in the blood vessels of patients with ALS schizophrenia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the endothelium of blood vessels is a target for the action of the pathogenetic factors in ALS schizophrenia.
the observed endothelial dysfunction in patients with ALS schizophrenia may be a result of a systemic inflammatory process.
EC dysfunction/lesion and blood-brain barrier dysfunction in ALS are caused by the increased activity of LE.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ALS schizophrenia is a multifactorial disorder in which the vascular component is of great importance.
ALS schizophrenia is accompanied with EC dysfunction and/or EC lesion.
in the blood plasma from ALS patients, the increased activity of elastase and the increased concentrations of C-RP and WF indicate the endothelial dysfunction in schizophrenia.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ALS patients should undergo an examination of vascular endothelium and blood-brain barrier in addition to the traditional clinical assessment.
ALS schizophrenia is a disease with a vascular component.
ALS is associated with endothelial dysfunction and vascular damage.
